svg.text: Hello Sello — the Build Pipeline, step by step
6 skills you type · 11 agents · the hooks · 5 gates where you decide — and the exact file every step writes
fresh context, one job, one artifact
the only agent that writes code
FOUR LANES — triage decides how much of the column below runs
FULL all 5 stages · STANDARD /spec --amend → /build → /ship · TRIVIAL /build → /ship · BUG /diagnose → /build → /ship
Any YES in triage pushes the lane up. Diff size is not the ruler — a one-line visibility change can leak data; a 200-line CSS refactor cannot.
and a hook checks it later.
six questions → lane: FULL · STANDARD · TRIVIAL · BUG
assigns the number + slug · opens the work folder
lane vs diff — fires later, at the diff: TRIVIAL touching migrations / RLS / auth → block, re-triage
STATE.md is the work order — lane · stage · branch · budgets · gate log. Every skill advances it as its last step (hook-enforced).
researcher — prior-art sweep: surfaces · PRDs · DECISIONS · Linear · the code
the interview — IN / OUT for v1 first (the fence), then edges, then how we'll know it works
writes the spec — every acceptance criterion checkable on a running page (EARS)
STATE.md advance — the skill cannot finish without advancing stage
Those acceptance criteria become the tests, and what G4 and G5 both walk. Write them once, use them three times.
reads the spec's fence — inside the IN / OUT list it can only explore, not wander
you pick one — taste is never delegated. The winner becomes the G4 visual contract
Open question (§14 #8): a standalone page cannot prove fit inside the real component — the 0021 popover redesign came from exactly this.
🚦 G2 — you pick a variant (frontend only)
researcher — which approaches exist, what each costs to undo later
the ADR — plain-English opening · Reused · Blast-radius · invariants
adr-checker — fresh context each round · 2 rounds, stop on zero NEW blockers · 9-category sweep
its output is claims to spot-verify, not verdicts — fixes carry a simplification bias
invariant sort — if a machine can check it, it leaves the prose
→ a lint rule or a test
Ready check — tickets INVEST · sized S/M/XS (bigger than M → split) · EARS · depends-on
one line in the index — an ADR not in the index does not exist
The ADR's invariants + the tickets' dependency order are what every /build below reads. Parallel tickets must touch different files.
🚦 G3 — you choose, from the plain-English section
plan — exact files · signatures · real test code
plan-checker — will this plan reach the goal? revise once, then STOP
test-writer — failing tests from the SPEC, never the code
builder — implements until green, only the files the plan names
test-runner — runs and reports, cannot edit · red → back to 4 · 2 rounds, then STOP
critic always · security if DB/auth · consistency if new pattern — in parallel, one message
findings are blocking | note · builder may reject in writing · ONE REVIEW.md per slug, every finding attributed: "(consistency)" · "(critic, migration:192)"
visual-verifier — drives the real page against the prototype (anything rendered)
Budgets, separate, in STATE.md: tests 2 rounds · blocking-findings 2 fix-ROUNDS (not findings) · a blown budget → blocked.md + you.
On a blowout the agent writes what it thinks is wrong with the instruction — it does not try harder.
The builder can disagree — a written rejection costs no attempt and lands in REVIEW.md for you to settle at G4.
🚦 G4 — you walk it vs the prototype · a redesign round never spends the cap
rebase onto dev FIRST → re-run the whole suite — touched a tested/rendered file → back to G4 (max 2)
PR → merge promptly → deploy — what you verified is what merges
prod data-write gate — a wave that UPDATEs / DELETEs prod data stops for YOUR allow rule (a scheduled stop, not a failure)
walk every acceptance criterion on the live URL — the same criteria the spec wrote
rollup — agent 11, fresh context · reads REVIEW.md + STATE.md + TICKETS.md, never the conversation
scores each agent twice — prediction landed? decisive catch? — quoting the artifacts · records what got NO workout
The slug cannot close until the roll-up exists. A verdict with no quotation behind it is not a verdict — the writer is never the checker.
The roll-up's verdicts are how the pipeline learns: they decide which agents stay, and which rules change.
🚦 G5 — live evidence closes the ticket, or it stays open
THE HOOKS — deterministic, 100% not 98% · they fire no matter which skill is running
lane vs diff — TRIVIAL diff touching migrations/RLS/auth → re-triage
STATE.md advance — a skill cannot finish without advancing stage
prod data-write gate — prod UPDATE/DELETE waits for your allow rule
invariant lint rules — whatever /design sorted machine-checkable
module boundary — module internals imported across modules
Supabase MCP schema guard — DDL with no committed .sql
destructive command guard — reset --hard · clean -fd · rm -rf …
stale-map — a new src/modules/ dir missing from src/README.md
shared-file lock — dormant · guards your own parallel worktrees
read-before-edit · conventional commits · main-branch write block ✅
ONE NUMBER · ONE SLUG NAMES EVERYTHING — numbers are identities, never reused. Example: 0007 · "pricelist"
PRD/0007-pricelist.md · architecture/adr/ADR-NNN-pricelist.md · muskan-build/0007-pricelist/ · prototypes/0007-pricelist-prototype/ · branch feature/pricelist
Permanent (never deleted, later work cites them): PRD/ · architecture/adr/ Disposable (archive when shipped): muskan-build/<slug>/ — STATE.md · TICKETS.md · PLAN-T0N.md · REVIEW.md · blocked.md
Walk from any file to every other file of the same feature by its number. That is the whole point.
